PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers reported to assess whether antibody-dependent cytotoxicity or zinc influx pathways were modulated. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint (ORR) clearly failed - Part A achieved 10% ORR, Part B achieved 11% ORR, both well below typical efficacy thresholds for advanced solid tumors. A partial signal was seen in PSA response rate (23%) in prostate cancer cohort. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Limited subgroup analysis showed some activity in prostate cancer (23% PSA response) but this was not the primary endpoint and represents a small subset. 5. CONFOUNDERS: No major trial design issues - adequate sample size (205 patients), long duration (162.8 weeks), appropriate dosing explored across multiple schedules. Study was terminated for portfolio prioritization, not safety.

failure_modes.evidence: Primary ORR endpoint failed across all arms (10-11%) despite some biological activity suggested by 23% PSA response in prostate cancer subgroup, indicating potential disconnect between target engagement and clinical benefit measurement
